items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Mayor McCabe opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

We would like to begin by acknowledging that the land on which many of us are gathered today is the land traditionally cared for by the Haudenosaunee, Anishnaabe and Neutral peoples. We also acknowledge the enduring presence and deep traditional knowledge and philosophies of the Indigenous people with whom we share this land today.
Mayor McCabe also shared thoughts on Council’s visit to Crow Shield Lodge.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Mayor McCabe provided Council with a moment of reflection.
At the beginning of this Council meeting, we pause to think about the needs of our community. May we show wisdom and compassion in all our decisions.

items.title: Zoning By-law Amendment Z-23-09,
notes: Canadian Tire Properties Inc.,
Report No.: IPPW2023-052
Prepared By: John Vos
Ward No.: Northwest, Ward 2
John Vos gave a presentation outlining the proposed development and zoning by-law amendments. He then responded to questions of Council.
At this time, Councillor Freeman declared a conflict with respect to the current item due to a conflict of interest relating to a family member’s employment and left the meeting.

Jonathan Rodger, Principal Planner, Zelinka Priamo Ltd. gave a presentation further detailing the proposed development, including the pedestrian connections, preliminary elevations, and the project highlights. They then responded to questions of Council.
As no one else was present to speak to the application, the Chair concluded the Formal Public Meeting and advised the application is now open to Council for a motion and debate.
Having previously declared a conflict, Councillor Freeman was absent for the taking of the vote.

items.title: Consideration of Notice of Motion Given at Previous Meeting
Affordable Housing Commitment Motion – Councillor Bodaly
notes: Councillor Bodaly introduced the motion and called on Adam Lauder to show examples of triplexes and fourplexes in the area.
Shiva Subramanian, Resident of Waterloo spoke in support of the motion and about the affordable housing crisis.
Nicholas Aboagye, Resident of Kitchener spoke in support of the motion and offered suggestions on what else the City can do to address the housing crisis.
Joel Cotter responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Questions
notes: Councillor Freeman asked staff if the City might consider starting a memorial banner program to honour veterans. Commissioner Ron Ormson spoke in support of this idea, and directed it to CAO, Tim Anderson.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Freeman wanted to inform Council that the 48th Squadron of 31 Combat Engineering Regiment - for the first time in the Canadian military history - would be interring their battle colours from the First World War on Saturday, November 4 at St.
Thomas Cemetery.

Councillor Vasic attended the Kitchener-Waterloo Art Gallery’s Black and Gold Gala on October 19, 2023. Bangishimo was the keynote speaker and Roshan James did some spoken word. Additionally, the Coalition of Muslim Women held their Radiant Ladies Night Gala on October 28, 2023. Lastly, the Lincoln Heights neighbourhood held their “Grave and Rave” neighbourhood event on October 29, 2023.

Councillor Bodaly mentioned that he and Mayor McCabe attended a Vista Hills Diwali event at RIM Park on Sunday, October 29, 2023. He specifically wanted to highlight the volunteers of the neighbourhood association who put the event on. There were over 250 people celebrating Diwali at the event.
Councillor Wright wanted to mention that the Mary Allen Farmer’s Market has concluded for the season, and that their annual general meeting is coming up.
Mayor McCabe shouted out the Sexual Assault Support Centre Gala happening on November 4, 2023.

motions.item_title: Affordable Housing Commitment Motion – Councillor Bodaly
motions.text: WHEREAS the City of Waterloo population increased by 15.7% between 2016 and 2021, faster than the provincial average of 5.8% and the national average of 5.2% during that same time period; and WHEREAS the City of Waterloo’s population is forecasted to grow by 45% to 185,000 people by 2051; and WHEREAS the City of Waterloo has committed to supporting the creation of 16,000 new housing units by 2031 as its Housing Pledge to the Province; and WHEREAS the City of Waterloo approved an Affordable Housing Strategy in June 2023 with 81 actions, that, among other things, recommended ways to increase housing supply and the diversity of housing options, with an emphasis on areas near transit and transportation corridors. WHEREAS the City of Waterloo currently permits up to three residential units per property as-of-right on a parcel of urban residential land; and WHEREAS the Government of Canada’s Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) grant program represents an opportunity for the City to review and accelerate actions to achieve more housing supply faster; and THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED: 1. That staff be directed to initiate an amendment to Zoning By-law 2018-050 to permit, as-of-right, up to four residential units and four storeys on residential parcels within low density residential zones, where appropriate (the “Amendment”) and report back to Council in Q1 2024; 2. As part of the Amendment, that staff be directed to identify appropriate zoning regulations and development criteria, considering matters such as safe access and servicing capacity, for Council’s consideration; and, 3. That Council confirm its support for the principle of intensification in transit supportive areas and near post-secondary institutions, and directs staff to identify opportunities to achieve the following planning objectives through the Official Plan Review, as recommended in the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy: a. higher density housing options in areas supported by transit and near post secondary institutions; and b. increase the supply of missing middle housing, evaluating opportunities for new missing middle corridors, modifications to the existing nodes and corridors strategy using a missing middle lens, and consideration of minimum height and density targets in specified areas to facilitate missing middle housing; 4. That Council reaffirm its commitment to our Affordable Housing Strategy, including the City of Waterloo’s goals to prioritize non- market housing, optimize existing housing, increase the supply of affordable housing, providing incentives to build new affordable housing, and enable a greater supply and mix of housing within our community. 5. That Council reaffirm its housing pledge of achieving the goal of 16,000 new homes by 2031, in partnership with the development industry. 6. That this motion be forwarded to the Hon. Sean Fraser, Minister of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities of Canada for consideration as part of our Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) grant application.
motions.text_html:
WHEREAS the City of Waterloo population increased by 15.7% between 2016 and 2021, faster than the provincial average of 5.8% and the national average of 5.2% during that same time period; and WHEREAS the City of Waterloo’s population is forecasted to grow by 45% to 185,000 people by 2051; and WHEREAS the City of Waterloo has committed to supporting the creation of 16,000 new housing units by 2031 as its Housing Pledge to the Province; and WHEREAS the City of Waterloo approved an Affordable Housing Strategy in June 2023 with 81 actions, that, among other things, recommended ways to increase housing supply and the diversity of housing options, with an emphasis on areas near transit and transportation corridors. WHEREAS the City of Waterloo currently permits up to three residential units per property as-of-right on a parcel of urban residential land; and WHEREAS the Government of Canada’s Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) grant program represents an opportunity for the City to review and accelerate actions to achieve more housing supply faster; and THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:

1. That staff be directed to initiate an amendment to Zoning By-law 2018-050 to permit, as-of-right, up to four residential units and four storeys on residential parcels within low density residential zones, where appropriate (the “Amendment”) and report back to Council in Q1 2024; 2. As part of the Amendment, that staff be directed to identify appropriate zoning regulations and development criteria, considering matters such as safe access and servicing capacity, for Council’s consideration; and,

3. That Council confirm its support for the principle of intensification in transit supportive areas and near post-secondary institutions, and directs staff to identify opportunities to achieve the following planning objectives through the Official Plan Review, as recommended in the City’s Affordable Housing Strategy: a. higher density housing options in areas supported by transit and near post secondary institutions; and b. increase the supply of missing middle housing, evaluating opportunities for new missing middle corridors, modifications to the existing nodes and corridors strategy using a missing middle lens, and consideration of minimum height and density targets in specified areas to facilitate missing middle housing;

4. That Council reaffirm its commitment to our Affordable Housing Strategy, including the City of Waterloo’s goals to prioritize non- market housing, optimize existing housing, increase the supply of affordable housing, providing incentives to build new affordable housing, and enable a greater supply and mix of housing within our community.

5. That Council reaffirm its housing pledge of achieving the goal of 16,000 new homes by 2031, in partnership with the development industry.

6. That this motion be forwarded to the Hon. Sean Fraser, Minister of Housing, Infrastructure and Communities of Canada for consideration as part of our Housing Accelerator Fund (HAF) grant application.
